checks.claim: C1: The parent model is in the original class, and P is an actual rank-one orthogonal Gaussian projection with the stated positivity properties.
checks.reason: Checked against H:homog in source-inputs.txt. With d=1 and Gamma(dx)=(1-a)|x|^{-1/2}dx, Gamma(cA)=c^{1/2}Gamma(A)=c^{d-alpha}Gamma(A), so alpha=1/2 lies in (0,d). Also alpha_0=a=99/100 lies in (0,1), and alpha+a=149/100<2. The positive factor 1-a is allowed because the class contains any nonnegative even PD tempered measure with this homogeneity. The mixture formula holds: int_0^inf v^{s-1}e^{-vx^2}dv=Gamma(s)|x|^{-2s}, and s=1/4 gives Gamma(1/4)^{-1}int v^{-3/4}e^{-vx^2}dv=|x|^{-1/2}. A positive mixture of Gaussian PD kernels is PD, the kernel is locally integrable with polynomial growth, and so it is tempered. psi=1_[0,1]x1_[-1,1] lies in the Hilbert completion: int int|psi psi C|<inf because a<1 and the exponent 1/2<1. Approximants bounded by 1 on a fixed compact set converge in the C-norm by dominated convergence. V=2E_phi/(2-a), about 14.94, is finite and positive, so Z=W(psi)/sqrt(V) has unit variance. m=E[W Z] is the Riesz representer of the unit vector psi/sqrt(V). P=m tensor m is therefore the covariance of the orthogonal projection Z*m, C-P is the covariance of the residual Wperp and is Loewner-PSD by Cauchy-Schwarz, and Wperp is independent of Z by joint Gaussianity and orthogonality. P>=0 pointwise because B_a>0 and F>0. The note does not infer pointwise positivity of C-P. In fact C-P is negative on the cone: for s=0, t=1, C<=0.01*2^{-1/2}... no, C is at least (1-a)/sqrt(2) on |x-y|<=2, about 0.007, while P>=8/V is about 0.535. This sign is consistent with the counterexample.

checks.reason: E_phi=2 int_0^2 (2-r)r^{-1/2}dr=2(4sqrt2-4sqrt2/3)=16sqrt2/3. The time integral is int int_[0,1]^2|s-t|^{-a}=2/((1-a)(2-a)), so V=(1-a)*2/((1-a)(2-a))*E_phi=2E_phi/(2-a). Next, int_0^1|s-t|^{-a}dt=(s^{1-a}+(1-s)^{1-a})/(1-a), so the factor 1-a cancels and m=B_a F/sqrt(V). For |x|<=1, F=2(sqrt(1+x)+sqrt(1-x)), and the squared sum is 2+2sqrt(1-x^2)>=2, so F>=2sqrt2, with maximum 4 at x=0. For |x|>1, F=2(sqrt(|x|+1)-sqrt(|x|-1)), which decreases from 2sqrt2, so F<=4 globally. Since 0<1-a<1, s^{1-a}>=s on [0,1], which gives 1<=B_a<=2. In the terminal n=2 kernel, |y|<1-t and |z-y|<t-s give |z|<1-s. Both vertices therefore lie in the backward cone of (1,0), inside [0,1]x[-1,1], where mm>=(2sqrt2)^2/V=8/V=4(2-a)/E_phi. The Green masses are 1-t and t-s, and int_{0<s<t<1}(1-t)(t-s)=(1/2)int_0^1(1-t)t^2=1/24. Hence A_P>=(2-a)/(6E_phi)=(2-a)/(32sqrt2)=101/(3200sqrt2). This exceeds 101/4800>1/48 because sqrt2<3/2. The argument uses the forward terminal kernel only: there is no time reversal, no factorial, and no initial-chain transplant.

checks.claim: C4: The full means under the retained-residual tilt satisfy (M), giving a strict full-mean failure for sufficiently small h.
checks.reason: L_q=q^{-1/2}exp((1-1/q)Z^2/2) is the N(0,q)/N(0,1) density ratio, and E L_q=1. Also E L_q^2=q^{-1}(1-2(1-1/q))^{-1/2}=[q(2-q)]^{-1/2}, which is finite iff q<2. Under the tilt, W=Zm+Wperp with Z~N(0,q) and Wperp unchanged and independent, so the covariance is qP+(C-P)=C+(q-1)P. The laws are mutually absolutely continuous, so the original a.s.-defined functional u_C is evaluated under an equivalent law, and no new existence theorem is used. For the geometric bound, P:mixed applied to the admissible covariance r^2C gives E u_C(r)^2 as a convergent sum of nonnegative terms that contains r^{2n}E X_n^2, using n-linearity of the chains. Hence ||X_n||_2<=sqrt(B_r)r^{-n}, and the tail bound (T) follows. Cauchy-Schwarz with ||L_q||_2 gives an L1 remainder O(h^4) that is uniform for |h|<=r/2. The sign flip W->-W preserves both laws, L_q is even and X_n is odd for odd n, so odd orders vanish. For E_Q X_2: E[L_q Y_2^{eps}]=A_{C_eps}+(q-1)A_{P_eps} by the positive-width Wick formula. The first term converges to A_C by parent L2 convergence. The profile part converges to A_P by dominated convergence, because the regularized profiles are bounded by sup m and converge pointwise (m is continuous) on a finite-mass kernel. For qP, the Picard coefficients satisfy |d_n|<=M^n/(2n)! from the mass of g_n, which is 1/(2n)!. The absolute series is bounded by E cosh(sqrt(M sqrt(q)|Z|))<inf for |h|<=1, so its tail beyond n>=4 is O(h^4). Odd terms vanish, and the degree-2 term is q E[Z^2]... evaluated as h^2 q d_2=h^2 q A_P. Hence E_Q u_C-E u_qP=h^2(A_C-A_P)+O(h^4)<-h^2/96+O(h^4)<0 for small h>0. No uniform numerical h threshold is claimed. At q=1 the same argument gives E_C u_C(h)<E u_P(h). Only C and h^2C are required to be admissible.

checks.claim: C5: The residual lower-bridge contract (F) is correct, and (H) is stated as an unproved sufficient condition.
checks.reason: For N orthonormal coordinates, the product density L has E L^2=[q(2-q)]^{-N/2}. Since E_Q u=E[Lu]<=||L||_2||u||_2, this gives (F) for each fixed 1<q<2. Assume (H) with N_T=o(T^kappa) and E_Q u eventually positive. Because log(q(2-q)) is a fixed finite number for fixed q, (N_T/2)log(q(2-q))=o(T^kappa), and so liminf T^{-kappa}log E u^2>=2(q^{1/(3-alpha)}ell-delta). Letting T->inf, then delta->0, then q up to 2 gives the factor 2^{1+1/(3-alpha)}*ell, where ell>0 is an independently valid first-mean lower constant. The exponent q^{1/(3-alpha)} agrees with the wave scaling for an amplified homogeneous covariance, lambda^{kappa/(4-alpha-alpha_0)}=lambda^{1/(3-alpha)}. Here it appears only inside the hypothesis (H) and is not applied as a theorem to Q or P. The note labels (H) as unproved and does not assume q(T)->2 or uniformity in q. It adopts no repair of the printed normalization, consistent with the source paragraph. The obstruction is scoped only to unconditional residual discard.

minor: Section 4 (T) cites L:uniform-series-tail, whose hypothesis is a uniform-in-regularization bound, but supplies only B_r=E|u_C(r)|^2<inf. The bound ||X_n||_2<=sqrt(B_r)r^{-n} follows directly from P:mixed applied to the admissible covariance r^2C, together with the n-linearity X_n^{(r^2C)}=r^n X_n^{(C)}. Stating this one-line route would remove the mismatch with the lemma's hypothesis.

Section 4 says the regularized projection profiles are 'mollifications of the bounded m'. The packet does not reproduce the source's exact noise-regularization operator. The step needs only that the regularization is a linear positive averaging map of W on the same probability space, so that the regularized profiles are bounded by sup m and converge pointwise to the continuous m. This should be stated explicitly.
The wording 'Positivity yields' for the geometric bound is terse. The positivity used is that of the mixed moments in the amplified series.

Lean-statement-fence.md says finiteness under the q tilt 'requires 1<q<2'. The condition E L_q^2<inf actually holds for all 0<q<2. The lower limit q>1 comes from the tilt consumer, not from finiteness. This is harmless.

Section 1 says the Gaussian mixture also works for the temporal power. This is true, since |t|^{-a}=Gamma(a/2)^{-1}int v^{a/2-1}e^{-vt^2}dv, but it is unnecessary because the temporal factor |s-t|^{-alpha_0} is fixed by the source model.
Section 5 should state explicitly that ell>0, so that sending q up to 2 is the optimal direction.
